title: Effect of Crosslinker and Nanoclay on Jute Fabric Reinforced Soy Flour Green Composite
source_version: Published journal article, 2013 issue; first published online 24 May 2012; publisher-formatted copy uploaded by author Murshid Iman on 27 March 2020
source_document_description: Indexed author-uploaded publisher-formatted original article; PDF bytes and figure pixels unavailable
source_material_form_TGA_raw: Finished soy-flour/jute composite laminates prepared by stacking impregnated jute fabric on 15 levels and compression moulding; whole-composite TG specified, aliquot handling unreported
TGA_specimen_preparation: The composite samples were tested under nitrogen at 30 mL/min and 10 °C/min from source-stated 0 to 600 °C. Mass, pan, cutting or grinding, through-thickness selection, separate conditioning and replication are unreported.
LOI_method: ASTM D-2863; S. C. Dey flammability tester, Kolkata; source records oxygen/nitrogen ratio at which the specimen continued burning for at least 30 s
LOI_uncertainty_type: Unresolved source glyph and uncertainty definition; raw parenthetical suffix retained
LOI_statistic: Printed central value with a parenthetical uncertainty-like suffix; averaging and replication are unreported
LOI_specimen_preparation: Prepared composite laminate; LOI dimensions, mounting and separate conditioning are unreported. The dimensional-stability humidity treatment is a separate experiment.
source_numeric_evidence_description: Own Table II final column RW% at 600 °C and own Table III measured LOI in the indexed author original. No PDF-pixel or graph-coordinate claim.
TG_locator: Measurements/Thermogravimetric Analysis, printed page 3989; Thermal Property Study on page 3992; Table II on page 3993
LOI_locator: Measurements/Limiting Oxygen Index, printed page 3989; Limiting Oxygen Index study on pages 3993–3994; Table III on page 3994
conditions_locator: Experimental/Materials and Methods, Impregnation of Jute Fabrics and Fabrication of Composites, printed pages 3988–3989; Table I on page 3989
source_location: Original journal pages 3987–3996; preparation pages 3988–3989, Table I page 3989, Table II page 3993 and Table III page 3994
washing_state: Initial manufactured laminate after jute washing, dewaxing, alkali treatment, repeated rinsing and drying; no durability wash, humidity-exposed or aged LOI/TG state assigned
treatment_method: Jute fabric was washed in 2% soap solution at 70 °C for 1 h, rinsed with distilled water and vacuum-dried at 100 °C for 12 h. It was dewaxed in alcohol/benzene 1:2 for 72 h at 50 °C, washed and dried for 12 h, then treated with 5% w/v NaOH for 30 min at 30 °C, repeatedly rinsed, immersed in distilled water overnight, rinsed again and vacuum-dried at 70 °C for 12 h before desiccator storage. Soy flour and deionized water were mixed 1:10 by mass and glycerol was added. The slurry was mechanically stirred for 4 h at source-stated 55 °C with an unresolved indexed uncertainty suffix, cooled to source-stated 35 °C with the same suffix and mixed with the specified GA amount for 5 min. For MMT states, clay was dispersed in water, magnetically stirred for 6 h and sonicated for 30 min at source-stated 0.5 cycle and 140 l m wave amplitude (unit as indexed) before addition to the pre-cured resin. Surface-modified fabric was dipped for 24 h at 25 °C, placed on a Teflon-coated glass plate and dried on a heating plate at 60–70 °C. Impregnated fabric was stacked on 15 levels in a 3 mm metal mould and compression-moulded in a Santec press at 80 °C and 100 MPa; pressing duration is unreported. The final laminate thickness is reported as 3 mm.
source_fabric_area_density_raw: 0.400 g/cm² as printed in indexed Materials; no unit correction or conversion adopted
source_reaction_temperature_raw: 55 °C 6 5 °C for 4 h; 35 °C 6 5 °C for GA addition, as indexed; the 6 glyph is unresolved without pixels
source_TableI_header_raw: Starch (wt%) with footnote: Twenty gram of soy flour is assumed to be 100.
source_GA_supply_raw: Glutaraldehyde supplied as 25% w/v; nominal formulation percentages and parenthetical grams are retained without converting to active GA content
source_residue_definition: Table II final column RW% at 600 °C; text calls it residual weight and correlates it with independently measured LOI. Whole finished laminate residue, not a precursor or a cone/MCC result.
source_Ti_definition: Initial decomposition temperature; onset criterion unspecified. Kept source-native only.
source_Tm_definition: Maximum pyrolysis temperature, first and second step. No explicit maximum-rate or DTG definition is established; kept source-native only.
limitations: The exact residue/LOI pairs use identical prepared laminate labels in Tables II and III. Three additional LOI labels have no TG row, and precursor soy flour and jute TG values are not substituted. The article is available as indexed author-uploaded original text; PDF bytes and figure pixels were not recovered. The final RW% column is explicit, but the Table II weight-loss-temperature columns are not unambiguously aligned in the indexed text and remain source-native. Initial decomposition temperatures have no stated onset criterion, and maximum pyrolysis temperatures have no explicit rate definition; neither is promoted to a canonical onset or DTG field. Parenthetical LOI suffixes contain an indexed 6 glyph; the raw entries are retained without assigning an SD, uncertainty type or replicate count. The ten-sample mean stated for flexural testing is not transferred to LOI or TG. Table I uses a Starch header despite its soy-flour footnote and the repeated soy-flour identity in materials, preparation and results; this inconsistency is preserved. Table I combines different formulation bases and is not normalized into a single whole-laminate composition. The source-reported fabric areal-density unit is retained without correction. Active GA amount is not inferred from the supplied 25% w/v stock. Pressing duration, weave, TG aliquot handling, mass, pan and replication, and LOI geometry/conditioning are unreported. Separate humidity swelling, FTIR specimen grinding and mechanical conditioning are not assigned to TG or LOI. Related later soy/jute nanofiller papers require control-level reuse assessment before repeated pairs are imported.
composition: Table I nominal formulation: soy flour 100 (20 g basis, under the printed Starch header); glycerol 5; GA 0; jute 75; MMT 0. GA and MMT are stated relative to soy flour. The jute-content equation uses pre-impregnation jute mass divided by final composite mass; mixed table bases are retained without renormalization.
treatment_chemistry: Soy flour/glycerol resin with nominal GA 0% and MMT 0% relative to soy flour, applied to washed/dewaxed/alkali-treated jute fabric
source_weight_loss_temperature_header_ra: 20 30 40 50 60 70%; five populated temperatures appear in each indexed row, so alignment is withheld
pairing_evidence: Table I identifies the finished laminate S/J; Table II gives its own nitrogen residual weight at 600 °C and Table III independently measures its LOI under the same initial preparation label. No precursor TG or computed residue-to-LOI relation is used.

For MMT states, clay was dispersed in water, magnetically stirred for 6 h and sonicated for 30 min at source-stated 0.5 cycle and 140 l m wave amplitude (unit as indexed) before addition to the pre-cured resin. Surface-modified fabric was dipped for 24 h at 25 °C, placed on a Teflon-coated glass plate and dried on a heating plate at 60–70 °C. Impregnated fabric was stacked on 15 levels in a 3 mm metal mould and compression-moulded in a Santec press at 80 °C and 100 MPa; pressing duration is unreported.
